subject: AI model training carveout — DPA redlines & signature order
message_1_headers:
From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@ellisonhealth.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@ellisonhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form — DPA carveouts
message_1_body:
Thanks Aditya — we reviewed the draft MSA and DPA and appreciate the quick turnaround. Two items are blocking our final signoff: 1) an explicit carveout preventing Redwood from using customer data for AI model training (we need a statement that training data will not be used without an explicit addendum), and 2) a clarified subprocessor onboarding process with evidence requirements.

I attached a short summary of the items we need (redline_dpa_v3.pdf). We can accept a limited exception if Redwood provides an auditable evidence bundle and a written commitment that training will only occur under a separate, signed Data Use Addendum.

Can you confirm the signature order you proposed? We prefer Ellison legal and InfoSec sign before any operational go-live.

—Sara
Senior Counsel, Ellison Health
message_2_headers:
From: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Draft MSA + Order Form — DPA carveouts
message_2_body:
Forwarding Sara's note — Ellison is calling out an AI training carveout and wants subprocessor evidence. Quick plan suggestion: (1) confirm we will not train on customer data without a signed Data Use Addendum (DUA), (2) offer an auditable evidence manifest (logs + KMS receipts + subprocessor attestations), (3) propose signature sequence: Ellison Legal -> Ellison InfoSec -> Redwood Legal -> Redwood Ops.

Ben: can you own commercial pushback on the carveout wording (we should avoid absolute prohibitions — propose 'no training without a separate written agreement that specifies noise injection / differential privacy options'). Laura: can you pull the minimal evidence bundle we can share (logs, subprocessors list, SOC-2 scope note)? Rishi: loop in Product if there are any technical blockers to providing attestations.

Goal: get to a one-page compromise and DocuSign link by Friday.

—Aditya
message_3_headers:
From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: legal@ellisonhealth.com, sara.klein@ellisonhealth.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-05T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form — DPA carveouts (proposed language)
message_3_body:
Hi Sara — thanks for the clear asks. We've drafted suggested language and attached a clean redline and an evidence manifest for your review (evidence_matrix.xlsx). Key proposals: 1) Add DPA Section X.Y: 'Redwood will not use Customer Personal Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve machine learning models without a separate Data Use Addendum executed by both parties.' 2) Subprocessor onboarding: Redwood will provide a quarterly manifest of subprocessors and upfront attestations for any subprocessors that will have access to Personal Data; for high-risk subprocessors we will provide a bridge letter within 5 business days. 3) Evidence bundle: we can provide KMS key usage logs, access logs for the relevant project IDs, and a SOC 2 scope statement.

We propose one small addition to make this operationally feasible: allow Redwood to provide redacted logs and aggregated attestations where disclosure of raw logs would breach vendor NDAs. We can add a verification step (Redwood legal + Ellison InfoSec) if needed.

If acceptable, we will prepare the DUA template that scopes training uses and technical mitigations (differential privacy, minimization). Also confirming the signature order below: Ellison Legal -> Ellison InfoSec -> Redwood Legal -> Redwood Ops. I'll attach a proposed signature order doc (proposed_signature_order.docx).

On Tue, Apr 6, 2027 at 09:15 AM Sara Klein <sara.klein@ellisonhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks — a quick follow-up: can Redwood commit to a 30-day notice window before any change to subprocessor access that materially increases exposure?
> 
> —Sara

message_4_body:
Laura/Aditya — thanks for the suggested language and the evidence manifest. That addresses most of our concerns. A few minor asks before we proceed to DocuSign: 1) add the 30-day notice requirement for material subprocessor changes into the onboarding clause; 2) include a narrow definition of 'material' (we proposed 'access to unredacted customer Personal Data or introduction of a new subprocessor with access to encryption keys'); 3) confirm that the DUA will include explicit technical mitigations we discussed.

If Redwood agrees, I'm ready to proceed — I'll send a DocuSign envelope (one set of signatories on our side). Please confirm your internal sign order and whether Redwood needs us to sign first.

DocuSign link (Ellison): https://docusign.com/Envelope/00A1B2C3D4

—Sara

message_5_body:
Sara — thanks, we agree to the 30-day notice and the proposed narrow definition of 'material'. Redwood confirms we will not use Customer Personal Data for model training without the signed DUA. We'll prepare the DUA template with the technical mitigations and proposed verification process.

Regarding signature order: we prefer Redwood Legal -> Redwood Ops -> Ellison Legal -> Ellison InfoSec, but we can accept Ellison signing first if that speeds execution. To avoid any confusion on go-live gating, can we do this: Ellison signs DocuSign envelope first, then Redwood completes our signatures within 48 hours and we publish a joint go/no-go checklist that includes evidence handoff items.

Ben: finalize the commercial caveats on the absolute 'no training' phrasing and confirm the redline we send back tonight. Laura: attach the evidence bundle to the DocuSign envelope as supplemental documents. Rishi: highlight any product limitations that would prevent providing the redacted logs.

I'll send the internal sign-off thread once Ben and Laura confirm. Thanks — looking forward to closing.

—Aditya
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
